title: Auditable Access Gate: Central PDP + lightweight enforcers for API, runtime, and console
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a central Access Gate (PDP: Policy Decision Point backed by a policy evaluation engine and attribute store) plus minimal per-environment Enforcer adapters (PEP) to enforce RBAC v2 across the Redwood API, inference runtime, and Console. This work focuses on end-to-end enforcement, consistent audit trails, SSO/SAML compatibility for admin role sync, and a migration path from the existing authorization checks to a centralized decision service with local caching for latency-sensitive paths.
acceptance_criteria: Central PDP service responds to evaluation requests with decision+metadata within 25ms P95 for cached attributes
Runtime enforcer adapter can perform local cached checks for token-scoped requests and fall back to PDP when cache miss occurs
Audit logs include actor, resource, action, decision, policy_id, attributes snapshot, and request trace id for every privileged decision
Console uses PDP for UI control shows and admin operations with role sync from SSO/SAML IdP
Feature flag controls per-tenant canary rollout of PD-based enforcement with automatic fallback to legacy checks
Automated tests cover policy evaluation correctness (positive/negative cases), cache coherence, and regression tests for existing routes
implementation_plan: Design PDP API: /v1/evaluate (attributes + resource + action) -> {allow|deny|conditional, policy_ids, reasons}
Policy language selection: adopt simplified Rego-like DSL or existing open-source evaluator; prototype both and pick based on runtime latency and policy expressivity
Attribute store: define attribute contract (user, roles, teams, tenant, request metadata) and implement a read-through cache with TTL and invalidation hooks from SSO sync
Enforcer adapters: build lightweight Go middleware for API gateway, C++ plugin for runtime fast-path, and React-level guard for Console UI (calls PDP only for admin checks)
Audit pipeline: extend existing logging to push structured audit events to Kafka with schema versioning and retention controls; wire to console incident dashboard
SSO/SAML integration: expand IdP sync to write canonical role/tenants mapping into attribute store and surface admin flag claims
Migration tooling: implement canary flags, per-tenant toggles, and a monitoring dashboard tracking decision mismatches vs legacy checks
Docs & runbooks: update runbook for incident response and escalation if PDP or cache causes auth regressions
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Internal: PDP in dev, enforcers in staging; run parallel logging against legacy checks to collect diffs
Phase 2 - Beta tenants: enable PDP for 2-3 low-risk customers using per-tenant flag; monitor false-deny/allow rates <0.1%
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp: auto-scale PDP and expand tenant coverage; hard switch only after 2 weeks of stable metrics
Fallback: Enforcers must be able to fall back to legacy check on PDP errors; circuit-breaker and degraded mode telemetry required
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluator: edge cases, attribute absence, and policy precedence
Load tests: 5k RPS PDP eval with 3ms median per-eval using synthetic policies and cached attributes
Chaos tests: PDP downtime simulation, cache-stale scenarios, SSO spike during role sync
E2E: Console admin flows, API admin endpoints, runtime inference control plane for model access
Audit verification: replay recorded audit events into offline validator to ensure required fields and immutability
